title: PalawanPay Trilogy Marathon 2026 Palawan Leg Review: Racing to the UNESCO River
meta_description: PalawanPay Trilogy Marathon 2026 Palawan Leg review: October 18 in Puerto Princesa -- five distances near a UNESCO World Heritage subterranean river.
dek: Set for 18 October 2026 in Puerto Princesa, this Palawan leg of the PalawanPay Trilogy Marathon runs in the same province as the Puerto Princesa Subterranean River -- a UNESCO World Heritage Site and New7Wonders of Nature.
verdict: The PalawanPay Trilogy Marathon's Palawan leg has an obvious geographic tie-in: the title sponsor is named for the province hosting a UNESCO World Heritage Site and New7Wonders of Nature finalist -- the Puerto Princesa Subterranean River. Five distances, including an unusual 16K alongside the standard spread up to the full 42.195K, give it real range. Puerto Princesa itself has been a settlement since Spanish colonists founded it in 1872, with its own airport making the province genuinely accessible despite its island-frontier reputation. Registration status wasn't yet confirmed open at the time of this research.

sections.heading: A Race Named for Its Province
paragraphs: The Palawan leg is organised by RUNRIO Inc. with title sponsor PalawanPay, offering five distances: 5K, 10K, 16K, 21.1K and the 42.195K full marathon. [1] The sponsor's name is a direct reference to Palawan province itself, and this leg puts the race squarely in the province's capital, Puerto Princesa.

sections.heading: Home to a UNESCO World Heritage Site
paragraphs: Puerto Princesa is the capital of Palawan province, founded by Spanish colonists on 4 March 1872, situated between the Sulu Sea to the east and the South China Sea to the west, with its own airport. [2] It's best known for the Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park -- a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1999 and voted one of the New7Wonders of Nature in 2012. Running a marathon in the same province as one of the world's most celebrated natural landmarks gives this leg genuine destination cachet beyond the race itself.

sections.heading: An Unusual 16K Distance
paragraphs: Alongside the standard 5K, 10K, 21.1K and 42K categories, this leg includes a 16K option -- an uncommon distance choice, similar to the 16K seen at the PalawanPay Trilogy's Cebu leg covered elsewhere in this research, likely tied to the broader Trilogy format's progressive qualifying structure.

sections.heading: Registration Not Yet Confirmed
paragraphs: As of this writing, registration status for the Palawan leg has not been confirmed open. [1] Given Palawan's popularity as a tourist destination generally, demand could be significant once registration opens -- worth watching official channels closely.

sections.heading: Should You Run It?
paragraphs: If you want to pair a marathon with a trip to one of the world's most celebrated natural wonders, the PalawanPay Trilogy Marathon's Palawan leg on 18 October 2026 offers genuine destination value beyond the race itself. Watch for registration to open before finalising travel plans.
